sections.html:
South of Tulsa, the suburb of Bixby is cut into north and south halves by the Arkansas River. The original town center is south of the river, and the city lies in both Tulsa and Wagoner counties. Population grew from 20,884 in 2010 to 28,609 in 2020, an increase of about 37 percent, and the city had only 1,711 residents in 1960. In 2020 there were 11,043 housing units with 5.4 percent vacant, and owners lived in 74.0 percent of occupied homes. Median age was 37.0 years. Bixby also holds a Green Corn Festival each June, a reminder that much of today's housing was once farmland.

Low vacancy and high owner occupancy describe a family market. Because of the rapid growth, many houses are fairly new, which can mean fewer foundation and wiring surprises and more questions about finishes, drainage and HOA covenants. Older homes cluster near the original streets, and newer subdivisions sit on former farmland and river-bottom ground, so soil movement, grading and drainage are fair inspection topics.

Bixby Public Schools serves the town, and part of Broken Arrow also falls in the Bixby district. Buyers with children ask about attendance zones, so confirm the exact boundary for your address.

Flooding along the Arkansas River and its creeks has been a real planning issue. The Haikey Creek levee was expected to bring 920 acres out of the floodplain, which addressed one of the last major flood-impaired areas north of the river. Even so, a buyer's lender may require flood insurance depending on the map, so check the current flood zone before you set a price. The Oklahoma Water Resources Board lists a floodplain administrator for Bixby.

  • Look up the parcel's flood zone before you list.
  • Gather any elevation certificate or past flood insurance claims.
  • Be ready to answer drainage questions about the lot, not only the house.

The City of Bixby's Public Works Authority supplies water, which comes from the City of Tulsa. The city's utility guide lists the providers for sewer, natural gas, telecommunications, electricity and trash. Trash service reaches residents north and south of the river and nearby communities such as Leonard and Liberty. Availability can differ north and south of the Arkansas River, so confirm which providers serve your address.

When you move out, schedule a final water reading and transfer or stop service on the closing date so the buyer does not inherit your charges.

Bixby handles code enforcement through its police department. The city's page explains what counts as a nuisance. A single blade of grass taller than 12 inches is not a violation. The tall growth must cover the majority of the yard, as estimated by code enforcement.

Development Services runs the building permit process and requires electrical, plumbing and mechanical work to be done by contractors registered with the city. If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a water heater, find the permit and final inspection records. A cash buyer will usually take a house as is, but missing paperwork is easier to sort out before you sign.

Homeowners association covenants are separate from city code. Buyers' agents often ask about HOA dues and restrictions, so collect your HOA documents early.

Tulsa County's assessor covers most of Bixby and sets each value as of January 1. A homestead's taxable value is limited to a 3 percent yearly increase, and other real property to 5 percent. Both limits fall away when title changes hands, which means the new owner's first bill may exceed yours. Buyers who quote the seller's number are often caught off guard.

Tulsa County dateWhat happens
January 1 to March 15Apply for most exemptions, including homestead
First Monday in AprilLast day for an informal appeal when no increase notice was mailed
May 31Board of Equalization adjourns unless extended to June 30
NovemberTreasurer mails tax bills

A valuation notice gives you 30 calendar days to file a written protest. The part of Bixby in Wagoner County is handled by that county's offices instead.

Open the Notice of Valuation the day it comes. The date printed on it starts a 30-calendar-day window for a written protest to the Tulsa County Assessor, and (918) 596-5100 is the number for questions. Informal appeals are the first step. When your value stayed the same and no notice went out, the informal deadline is the first Monday in April.

Before calling, pull together sales of comparable houses, contractor estimates and photographs. Storm or flood damage deserves a mention at the start, since it shapes what a fair figure looks like.

Whatever tax you still owe is usually paid out of your proceeds. Before listing, ask the county treasurer what the balance is today, and if your parcel is in Wagoner County, call that county's treasurer instead.

  1. Check which county's records apply to your parcel.
  2. Ask the treasurer to put the balance in writing.
  3. Dig out permits for any basement, deck or water heater project.
  4. Round up HOA documents and flood paperwork.

A house with deferred repairs can be hard to sell on the open market, since buyers' lenders ask for repairs before closing. A direct buyer will often take it as is.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Keep one folder for the sale. Drop in your newest tax statement, the deed, a Notice of Valuation if you got one, HOA paperwork and permit records for any basement, deck or water heater work. A lot that has held water before needs flood insurance claims and an elevation certificate too.

Many Bixby buyers come from the Tulsa side of the river, and a house prepared to answer questions about taxes, drainage and school lines sells with fewer surprises. If repairs are needed, an as-is cash offer sidesteps the list a lender would write, and listing remains an option if the numbers look better.

One timing note: when you sell between November and spring, ask whether the current bill is paid, and tell your buyer that homestead applications are taken from January 1 to March 15.

Under 68 O.S. section 3201, the state taxes a conveyed deed at 75 cents per $500 of price, paid through the county clerk at recording.

Oklahoma also requires one- and two-unit sellers to hand the buyer either a condition disclosure or a disclaimer statement, as set out in 60 O.S. section 833 and the Real Estate Commission's forms. Whichever you choose, deliver it in writing.

faqs.q: Which county is my Bixby house in?
faqs.a: The city straddles Tulsa and Wagoner counties. Your tax notice names the one that applies, along with its assessor and clerk.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Bixby house if it is in a floodplain?
faqs.a: Yes. Flood zone status affects insurance and lending for a conventional buyer, which is why a cash sale can be simpler. Look up the parcel's current flood zone before discussing price.

faqs.q: What does Bixby code enforcement look for?
faqs.a: Violations such as overgrown yards that cover most of the lot. One tall blade of grass is not a violation. Check the city's code page for the full list.

faqs.q: Who pays Oklahoma documentary stamps when a house is sold?
faqs.a: The statute reaches anyone who signs or sells the deed, and both parties can be held responsible. Your contract states who pays at closing.

faqs.q: How soon can I protest a Tulsa County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the date on the Notice of Valuation to file a written protest with the Tulsa County Assessor. Call (918) 596-5100 for help.
